units.translation: Others say that Perseus, having cut off the Gorgon's head, flew over Libya, and from the drops of blood that fell were born wild beasts; for this reason he called Libya rich in wild beasts (1561). The same is said by Lycophron in the Alexandra (838).
b. To the king: to Polydectes or to Dictys. Gᵍ Sᵐ
1523. Hyperbion: meaning 'grievously and violently'. It is written: 'since no grievous wound distressed him'. Lᵐ P
1524. Coma: death. Sᵐ
1532. With bronze: they dug with bronze scoops, that is, they excavated. Lᵐ (P)
1533. The mattock signifies the two-pronged hoe. P
1536. Having proper burial: meaning 'having received'. 'Poured earth' in Homeric fashion means the earth heaped over the dead.
1537. Of the blowing wind: of the wind blowing. Lᵍ (P)
1543. With a whiz: meaning 'with a whistling'.
1544. Sparks: sparks. Sparks are flashes of light. Lᵐ (P)
1545. Clefts are the fissures in the earth. Lᵐ (Sᵐ) (P)
1549. Propitiatory gifts: gifts able to appease, expiatory offerings. Lᵐ (P)
1552. Pindar also in the Pythian Odes, in the ode to Arcesilaus (IV 20 sq.), mentions the appearance of Triton. It is found among those who have written about Cyrene and Libya. Lᵐ P

1558. For my father made me a witness: meaning 'judge'. But when Homer says of Agamemnon (Il. 23.486) 'witness Agamemnon son of Atreus', he means 'witness', 'guardian of the covenant'. Here he means 'overseer', 'scout'.
1561 a. In sheep-nurturing Libya: meaning 'born of sheep-nurturing Libya'. L
b. It is written both 'beast-nurturing' and 'sheep-nurturing'. P

c. Eurypylus of Libya: Eurypylus was the son of Poseidon and Celaeno, daughter of Atlas, and king of Cyrene. Phylarchus in the seventh book (81 F 15 J.) calls him Eurytus, and records his brother Lycaon. Acesander in the first book of his work On Cyrene (F 4 M. IV 285) says that after him Cyrene, daughter of Hypseus, ruled Libya. Callimachus also mentions Eurypylus, saying (Hymn 2.92) 'the destroyer of cattle, Eurypylus', when speaking of Cyrene.

1562-63 a. Willingly he held out: he made Euphemus receive the clod because of kinship, since he was the son of Poseidon and Europa, daughter of Tityus. And Eurypylus, into whose land they came, is also a son of Poseidon. It is also said by Pindar (Pyth. 4.22) that Euphemus received the clod.
b. And such things in reply: Palamedes from a counter-argument or by deception, but here from an answer.

1564 a. Attic land and sea: it is written 'Apian land and Minôan sea'. Apis is an island lying before Crete; the Minôan sea is before Crete, for this was the kingdom of Minos; or because he ruled the sea and made the islands subject to him. After the Cretan sea comes the Egyptian sea.
